lessons: Review found two fixable oversights in an approach that was otherwise sound. Redo the whole change from the merge base: the config.yaml exemption in dirty_overlap, plus the save, restore-to-HEAD, merge_squash and merge-file --ours reapply in write_squash in clutch/merge.py.

In write_squash, if the merge-file reapply raises after merge_squash, write the owner's original config.yaml bytes back before re-raising, as the merge_squash failure branch does. Or remove the saved merge-config-local only after the reapply succeeds. Never lose the owner's edit.
In tests/unit/test_merge_config_local.py, add a case where the fake merge-file raises. Assert that config.yaml afterwards equals the owner's original bytes.

In tests/unit/test_merge_config_local.py, assert the full merge-file argv: ("merge-file", "--ours", str(state/merge-config-local), str(state/merge-config-base), str(config)). This pins the owner-wins flag and the current/base/other order, not just the command names.

Keep the parts review found sound: act only when status_porcelain shows a tracked modification of config.yaml; give the test_merge_index_hook.py stand-in only status_porcelain=AsyncMock(return_value=''); add no tests to test_daemon_composition.py.
